previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and a history of venous thromboses presented with hypotension following hemodialysis, during which she reportedly lost 7 kg of fluid. She experienced headache and visual spots but remained alert and mentating well. Initial blood pressure was 86/55 mmHg, which improved with intravenous fluids. Evaluation showed no evidence of sepsis, cardiogenic shock, or acute cardiac ischemia. Labs and chest imaging were unremarkable except for mild vascular congestion. Blood pressure variability suggested possible cuff inaccuracies, with leg measurements being more reliable. Chronic left arm and leg pain were evaluated with X-rays of the left hip and shoulder, which showed degenerative changes but no acute fractures. All home medications, including warfarin and insulin, were continued unchanged. The renal team coordinated with the dialysis center to limit future ultrafiltration to prevent recurrence. The patient stabilized and was discharged to extended care with instructions to monitor daily weight and follow up on musculoskeletal imaging.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism

AP SUPINE CHEST, ___ AT 16:51 HOURS

FINDINGS:  The study is somewhat limited secondary to positioning.  The
patient is markedly rotated.  Again seen is a large-bore dual-lumen catheter
from a left subclavian approach.  Elevation of the right hemidiaphragm is
again evident and slightly exaggerated.  There is engorgement of the vascular
pedicle and cephalization of the pulmonary vascularity, which is likely at
least in part due to the supine positioning.  Linear atelectasis is seen in
the retrocardiac left lower lobe.  No focal consolidation is seen.  The
mediastinum again demonstrates a tortuous aorta exaggerated by the rotation. 
Likewise, the cardiac silhouette is stable, but exaggerated.  No large
effusion is noted.  Blunting of the right costophrenic angle is relatively
stable.  There is no pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:  Limited study, but overall grossly stable.  The slight
engorgement is noted principally in the left hilar region may be in part due
to recumbency.

with nausea, vomiting and focal left lower quadrant pain.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were acquired from the lung bases through the pubic
symphysis following administration of intravenous contrast.  Multiplanar
reformations were generated.

the exception of linear atelectasis and/or scarring on the left and trace
dependent atelectasis on the right.  The heart is top normal in size without

INDICATION: ___ year-old woman with choledocholithiasis and suspected
cholangitis. PTBD has been requested. Additionally, she has renal failure and
is dialyzed via a left femoral temporary hemodialysis catheter. The catheter
is not functioning well, and exchange has been requested.

OPERATORS:  Drs. ___ (fellow physician) and ___
(attending physician).  Dr. ___ was present throughout the procedure.

TECHNIQUE:

Informed consent was obtained after explaining the benefits, risks, and
alternatives.  The patient was positioned supine on the imaging table in the
interventional suite.  Timeout was performed as per ___ protocol.

Initial scout fluoroscopic image showed the tip of the old left femoral
dialysis catheter in the left iliac vein.  Under aseptic conditions and after
withdrawing about 5 cc from each of the ports of the left femoral temporary
hemodialysis catheter, a 0.035 inch ___ wire was advanced through the VIP
port and into the lower IVC. The catheter was removed over the wire.  Under
fluoroscopy, a 14 ___ dilator was used to dilate the tract, and a 14 ___
peel-away sheath was placed.  After removing the inner dilator and wire, a new
14 ___, 24 cm temporary hemodialysis catheter was placed via the sheath,
which was then peeled away.  The ports were aspirated and flushed.  The
catheter was secured by 0 silk sutures.  The catheter tip was noted under
fluoroscopy to be in the expected location of the left common iliac vein.  The
site was sterilely dressed.

Attention was now directed to the right upper abdomen.  Under aseptic
conditions and sonographic guidance, a 21-gauge Cook hollow-bore needle was
placed into the right anterior biliary system after a few attempts.  Sterile
contrast material was gently injected through the needle to opacify the
central biliary ducts.  Since the needle access site was relatively central,
another 21-gauge hollow-bore needle was placed in a right posterior biliary
duct more peripherally under fluoroscopic guidance.  A 0.016 inch Headliner
wire was passed via the needle and into the CBD.  The needle was exchanged
over the wire for an AccuStick system, which was appropriately advanced over
the metallic stiffener. Both metallic and plastic stiffners were then removed
along with the wire.  A 0.035 inch Glidewire was advanced through the
AccuStick sheath and into the duodenum.  The AccuStick sheath was then removed
to place a 6 ___ ___ sheath.  The inner cannula was removed.  The
Glidewire was then exchanged for an Amplatz wire.  A 5 ___ Kumpe catheter
was placed over the wire and within the sheath to direct the wire into the
distal duodenum.  The Kumpe catheter was removed. A small amount of bile was
withdrawn from the sidearm of the sheath for culture and sensitivity. Pullback
cholangiogram was performed by gently injecting contrast through the sidearm
of the sheath.  The sheath was then removed to dilate the tract with a 9
___ dilator under fluoroscopy.  An 8 ___ internal-external drain was
then placed over the wire and under fluoroscopy. A small amount of contrast
material was injected after forming the pigtail catheter in the duodenum by
gently withdrawing the string.  The catheter was gently withdrawn to
appropriately place the radiopaque marker.  The string was locked and trimmed.
The catheter was flushed with a small amount of saline and connected to an
external bag.  The catheter was secured by 0 silk sutures and StatLock.  The
site was appropriately dressed.  No immediate post-procedure complications
were seen.

FINDINGS:

No intrahepatic ductal dilatation. Mildly dilated right biliary duct. 
Significantly dilated CBD.  Multiple filling defects within CBD, likely
represent calculi. Slow passage of contrast from the biliary system into the
duodenum.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Exchange of the left femoral temporary hemodialysis catheter with a new 14
___, 24 cm temporary hemodialysis catheter. The line is ready for use.
2.  Placement of an 8 ___ internal-external biliary drainage catheter via a
right posterior biliary duct with its retention pigtail loop in the duodenum.

INDICATION:  Requirement of conversion of a temporary left femoral
hemodialysis line to a tunneled line.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___, Dr. ___ Dr. ___ attending who was

PROCEDURE:  
Following a detailed discussion regarding the risks and benefits of the
procedure, signed informed consent was obtained from the patient.  The patient
was brought to the angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table. 
The left groin and existing femoral temporary hemodialysis catheter were
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A pre-procedural timeout was
performed using three separate identifiers.

Moderate sedation was achieved using 50 mcg of fentanyl distributed across
total intraservice time of 25 minutes.  The patient's hemodynamic parameters
were continuously monitored by radiology nurse.  Local anesthesia was achieved
using 1% bicarbonate buffered with lidocaine and a lidocaine/epinephrine
mixture.

Both lumens of the existing temporary line were aspirated easily.  A 0.035
Amplatz stiff wire advanced through the distal port into the right atrium. 
Measurements were made for the new catheter.

Following local anesthetization, a 0.5-cm incision was made at the new tunnel
exit site 5-6 cm inferior and lateral to the venotomy site.  A 15.5 ___
dual-lumen hemodialysis catheter was advanced subcutaneously from the tunnel
exit site to the venotomy site with a metal tunneling device.  The temporary
line was removed over the wire and exchanged for 14 ___ dilator, then a 16
___ peel-away sheath.  The inner stylet and wire were removed.  The
catheter was advanced through the peel-away sheath.  The sheath was then
removed.

A final spot fluoroscopic image shows the tip of the new hemodialysis catheter
within the upper IVC.  Of note, this is the longest catheter available, with a
tip-to-cuff length of 50 cm.  

The new line was secured with 0 silk sutures.  The venotomy site was closed
with a single buried subcuticular stitch with ___ Vicryl.  Dry sterile
dressings were applied. Both ports aspirated and flushed easily.  The patient
tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate post-procedure
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Successful conversion of an existing left femoral hemodialysis
line to a tunneled dual-lumen 15.5 ___ hemodialysis catheter, terminating
at the upper IVC.  The tip-to-cuff length is 50 cm.  The line is ready for
use.

NO OVA AND PARASITES SEEN.  This test does not reliably detect Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora or Microsporidium. While most cases of Giardia are detected by routine O+P, the Giardia antigen test may enhance detection when organisms are rare.
